mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing output and economic expansion, which typically translates to improved corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 9.5% indicates a deteriorating labor market, which is associated with reduced consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate is below 0.5% and the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 0.5%, it indicates an imminent monetary tightening cycle, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (characterized by strong GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals an impending economic slowdown, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST declines in late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% indicates rising inflation, which typically prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual change exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak job growth (PAYEMS < 50.0 thousand) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.0%) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher current level of retail sales (RSAFS) reflects robust consumer demand, which typically translates to stronger corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index below 90.0 indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes reduced corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 90.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
